evidence.quote:
``json`` was added to Python 2.6, so the main reason to use ``simplejson`` is backwards compatibility with Python 2.4+ (although, as someone who occasionally has to maintain Python 2.4 code, the sooner it dies the better).

Considering the oldest test suite on this project runs on Python 2.7, it seems a good candidate to refactor this.
evidence.interpretation: A 有完整候选但预算用尽，片段排序影响可见性

evidence.quote: Yeah, I'm fairly ok with this once we drop Python 2.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote:
Removes simplejson in favor of Python's built-in json module. Since `itsdangerous.json` would just be an alias for that module now, it's replaced with an proxy that raises a deprecation warning on use.

closes #146
evidence.interpretation: 两组都可见

cases.question: 项目历史上有哪些被拒绝的特性提案及理由？

evidence.quote:
Howdy!

I've added marrow.templating support; one simple function, an entry point, and no additional dependencies.

Additionally, dump[s] commands now accept additional keyword arguments which are then passed to json.dumps, allowing you to control the serialization formatting.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote: I don't want to step into that particular direction with the library for the time being. Instead why not have a second library that implements the entrypoints for marrow if that is necessary? I still remember the last attempt of an unified templating language API and it was horrible, I don't want to be involved with that a second time.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote:
Especially since this is based on Django's signing module.

Alternatively, you could let us set a default secret key to use, which would be the more generally useful implementation.

It's just not very DRY to pass this information in everywhere that you use a signer in your code.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote: Itsdangerous is a separate library and has nothing to do with django.  Definitely not going to add magic that kicks in if the library is used in a certain environment.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote: I am familiar with the attack.  Itsdangerous signs, it does nothing else.  Whatever SSL does it out of the focus of this library.  Add a random salt to your data payload if you want to defeat that.  I believe that this issue should be solved on the SSL layer and not in itsdangerous.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote: Hmm. Wondering if that is a problem or not.  The only thing that you changed is the transport format, not the payload.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote: I don't see this as a security issue as the whole point of itsdangerous is to verify a payload was not modified.  We do this by creating a signature that, theoretically, only a trusted user can produce.  In my mind, unless this makes it easier for an attacker to forge signatures or create new signatures based on existing ones, I don't see it as a security threat.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote: OK, so probably this issue can be closed safely.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote: ACK, should be closed.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote:
Well, it might be desirable to differentiate between expired signatures and completely invalid ones. Technically, a signature can't be invalidated by time, either it's valid or it's not. The timestamp is additional payload that is evaluated after the signature proved to be valid.

Note that `TimestampSigner.validate` also raised `BadTimeSignature` which isn't caught either.

I would close this.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote: if the token is about to expire, I want to call an interface (or any one can point me in correct way) to extend the expiry time of an already issued token. I am using TimedJSONWebSignatureSerializer to create the tokens.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote: It's impossible to provide a facility like that because the expiration time is in the token itself. When you change any value in the token, you get a completely different token. An alternative implementation would be to issue a refresh token that won't expire and use that to issue new primary tokens.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote: I find JWT tricky to use securely which is why I avoid it like the plague whenever I can for my own stuff.  You cannot avoid JWT much for external interoperability obviously but I will not deprecate itsdangerous as a result :)
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote: Closing due to merge conflicts.  Also, rst uses double backticks for inline code.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote: Command seems to work without this.  Thanks for pointing it out though.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote: I timed both versions and there was no significant change, so just going to close this and leave it as is.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote: I'm on board with the exception fix, but why is there an unrelated change that makes invalid data into valid tokens?
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote: This is a good case for writing your own Serializer subclass.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote:
It's not unrelated, but I guess the PR's name implies a smaller scope.

Characters that are invalid base64 are first ignored, then decoding proceeds. Decoding could still fail because of bad data, though.
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选

evidence.quote: That's not something that should happen.  Invalid data is invalid, the fact that removing some characters might produce a valid signature doesn't matter.  If that's something you want to happen, write a custom Serializer subclass (although you should probably fix the thing sending you bad data instead).
evidence.interpretation: A 没有覆盖该区间的候选
